Engine: Get-InstallSnapshot (scanner.ps1) reads Run hives, top-level Program Files/ProgramData/AppData directories, uninstall keys and services; read-only, so the 'install-snapshot' action is reachable in Audit Mode on purpose - 'what did that installer change' is an audit question and gating it behind elevation would give the honest answer only to users who had already granted more power.

Diff is lib/snapshot.js, pure and injected nothing: the engine takes readings, this decides what a reading MEANS. Three decisions that a naive diff gets wrong, each with an assertion: a case-only path rewrite is not a change (Windows paths are case-preserving, not case-sensitive); an unreadable category reports ZERO removals rather than 'everything was deleted', and says so in the summary; output is sorted so two identical installs read identically instead of following OS enumeration order. Additions lead the summary and removals follow, because a user watching an install does not expect to be told about deletions and reads that as an alarm.

attributionPaths() is the payload bu2 needs: added directories only (registry entries are not paths and carry no bytes), recorded to the oplog as install-snapshot-diff so a path's owner is FACT rather than heuristic.

The 'before' reading is held in the main process, not the renderer, so a reload cannot lose it, and it deliberately survives a failed second reading so the user retries instead of losing the session - the error message says so.

DESIGN DEVIATION, recorded in lib/attribution.js's header: the plan called for MFT enumeration via FSCTL_ENUM_USN_DATA. USN records carry FileReferenceNumber, ParentFileReferenceNumber, FileName and FileAttributes but NOT size, so sizing that way means parsing raw $MFT records off the volume. Inverted the design instead - attribution is milliseconds and measurement is the expensive part, so classify FIRST and measure ONLY what classification could not explain. The fast path stopped being necessary rather than being reimplemented.

Honesty rule enforced by the module and by 36 assertions: 'unattributed' and 'orphaned' are different claims. Orphaned is positive - we watched the install and the program is gone - and is ONLY ever made on zrw's recorded evidence. A recorded path whose owner was never resolved (an installer that writes no uninstall entry) stays unattributed; calling it orphaned would invent the fact that makes the word mean anything. Unmeasured folders report null and a reason, never 0 B.

TWO DELIBERATE CHANGES FROM THE DESIGN AS FILED, both about not overclaiming:

An unelevated process cannot write HKLM under any circumstances, so running the probe from Audit Mode would report 'locked by policy' on every ordinary home machine in the world - confident, plausible, and completely wrong, which is the exact failure mode this issue exists to prevent. 2. It writes a SCRATCH value (VanishWriteProbe) and removes it in a finally block, rather than setting and reverting EnableLUA as the design suggested. Same key, same ACL, same answer, but a failure halfway through leaves a stray registry value instead of a machine with UAC switched off. test/uac-lock-verify.js asserts nothing in the engine ever writes EnableLUA.

WORDING IS PART OF THE CONTRACT and is asserted, not just written: the message must say 'likely', must never assert Group Policy did this (Windows does not record policy-origin on these values), must point at the administrator, and must NOT repeat the personal-machine advice. The unmanaged case still says 'turn UAC back on'.
